statement: At the start of your turn you control 7 Gig dice. You ready your cards and draw first, and only then does the game check whether you win.
why: 1.10.1: the game checks "before the first step of your Start Phase (the Ready Step)."

statement: An effect says Draw 2 with 1 card left in your deck. Do you draw that card and the game simply goes on?
why: 1.14.1: "the first card you cannot draw counts as drawing from an empty deck", and you lose immediately.

statement: An effect says Search 3 while your deck holds only 2 cards. Searching does not make you lose the game.
why: 11.17.3: you "search as many cards as you can (2), but you do not immediately lose".

statement: Both players reach a win condition at the same moment in the middle of an effect. Is the game a tie?
why: 1.13.1: "If both players win simultaneously, the game is considered a tie."

statement: An effect reads "you may draw 1, then trash 2." Can you decline the draw and still resolve the trash part?
why: 2.1.1: "If an effect includes 'you may,' you may choose not to resolve that part of the effect." The rest still resolves.

statement: A Unit's card text says it can attack ready Units, which the rules normally forbid. The card text does not override the attack-target rule.
why: 2.5: "If a card's text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules."

statement: A rival Unit with [ADRENALINE] is played while you control a Unit whose text says rival Units can't attack the turn they're played. Can the rival Unit attack that turn?
why: 2.6: "the preventing effect always takes precedence"; the rule's own example is this case.

statement: Your Unit has power 2 and an effect gives it -3 power. When it fights, it is treated as power 0, not -1.
why: 2.10.1: a negative value "is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values."

statement: Your Legend has a null ( - ) cost. Can you pay that cost to play it to the field?
why: 3.11.2.1: "You cannot pay a null cost." 4.5.3: such Legends "cannot be played to the field."

statement: An effect plays a Unit from your trash and says nothing about cost. You play it without paying.
why: 3.11.1.1: from any area "you must pay the card's cost unless an effect explicitly tells you to play it 'for free'".

statement: A face-up Legend without a Sell Tag cannot be spent for 1 €$.
why: 5.7.2.2: "If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$."

statement: You have 3 face-down Legends. Only one of them may be spent toward a single cost.
why: 5.7.2: "You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down."

statement: A Gear equipped to your Unit has the tag CYBERWARE. Does your Unit gain the CYBERWARE tag?
why: 4.11.3.2: "A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it."

statement: You equip Mantis Blades (power 2) to a Unit with printed power 3. The Unit's power is now 5.
why: 3.17.2: power "is equal to the power printed on the card plus the power of its equipped Gear"; 3 + 2 = 5.

statement: An effect gives all friendly Units +1 power this turn. A Gear equipped to one of those Units does not get +1 power from it.
why: 3.17.3.3: "A Gear's power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear."

statement: A Legend is removed from the game during play. Your deck's RAM Limits do not change.
why: 3.20.6: "If a Legend is removed from the game during play, your deck's RAM Limits are not affected."

statement: Your Legends give 0 Blue RAM, but an effect lets you play a Blue card. Does RAM stop you from playing it?
why: 3.20.6.1: "RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it's legal to include in your deck."

statement: A Legend is on your field as a Unit. Is it both a Unit and a Legend?
why: 4.2.1: "Legends on the field are both Units and Legends."

statement: An effect returns one of your Legends from the field to your hand. The Legend is removed from the game.
why: 4.4: hand is an invalid area; 4.4.1: "If a Legend moves to an invalid area, remove it from the game."

statement: Your face-down Legend is spent in the Legends area. You pay its cost to play it to the field. It enters ready.
why: 4.5.1: it "enters in the same orientation as it was when it left the Legends area", so it enters spent.

statement: You play a Unit from your hand. Can it attack this turn without any effect granting that?
why: 4.7: Units enter with Lag; 9.3.1.1: "Lagging Units can't attack."

statement: You have no Units on the field and only face-down Legends. Can you play a Gear?
why: 4.10: you must "equip it to a friendly Unit or friendly face-up Legend"; none exists, so the play is invalid.

statement: Your Unit already has 4 Gears equipped. Equipping a fifth would break the Gear limit.
why: 4.10.3: "There's no upper limit on the number of Gears equipped to a single Unit."

statement: A Unit does not inherit the text in the bottom textbox of a Gear equipped to it.
why: 4.11.3: "The bottom textbox contains effects inherited by the Unit or Legend the Gear is equipped to."

statement: An equipped Unit is returned to your hand. Next turn you play the Unit again. Does the Gear come back onto the field with it?
why: 4.12.1: in the hand "the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit... if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it."

statement: You paid for a Program and are resolving it. While it resolves, the Program is not in your hand or your trash.
why: 4.14.2: it "is considered outside of your hand, field, trash, or any other game area until you finish resolving its effects".

statement: You may rearrange the order of the cards in your own hand.
why: 5.4.2: "you can freely view its contents and change the order of cards in it."

statement: Can you ask how many cards are in your Rival's hand?
why: 5.4.4: "You may always know the number of cards in your Rival's hand."

statement: You can count how many cards remain in your Rival's deck at any time.
why: 5.5.5: "The total number of cards in your deck is public information and can be counted at any time."

statement: You have 9 Units on your field. Is your field at its Unit limit?
why: 5.6.5: "There is no limit on the amount of Units you can have in the Field area."

statement: You are holding 14 cards at the end of your turn. Must you discard down to a hand limit?
why: 5.4.5: "There is no limit to the number of cards allowed in your hand."

statement: You already used Sell for Turn this turn. A card effect tells you to sell a card. Can you still sell that card?
why: 5.8.2.3: "There is no limit to the number of cards you may Sell through card effects in a turn. (Only the Main phase Sell action is limited...)"

statement: Gig dice still in your fixer area do not count toward your Street Cred.
why: 5.10.3: fixer dice "don't count as friendly Gigs, nor towards your Street Cred."

statement: Your Rival's Gig area is empty. Is it a valid attack target?
why: 9.3.2.2: "An empty Gig area is not a valid attack target."

statement: Your Gig area is empty and an effect checks whether your Street Cred is less than 0. Is Null treated as smaller than 0?
why: 5.11.4.2: "When compared to 0, Null is the smaller number."

statement: A card removed from the game cannot re-enter the game unless an effect specifically returns it.
why: 5.13.2.2: "A card removed from the game cannot re-enter the game area unless an effect specifically returns the card to the game."

statement: Your d6 shows 5. Is it a max Gig?
why: 6.3.2: a max Gig is "at its highest possible value"; a d6's highest is 6 (6.3.3).

statement: Your d4 is at 1 and an effect says to set it to its min value. Does the d4 change?
why: 6.4.3: "A Gig's value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has. If an effect tells you to do so, the effect fails."

statement: An effect tells you to set your d6 to 8. Can you do that?
why: 6.5.1: "You cannot set a Gig to a value that isn't on its face (i.e. set a d6 to 8)."

statement: Your d4, d6 and d8 all show 3. How many value-pairs do you have? Two.
why: 6.6.1: "A Gig can only count towards a single value-pair at a time"; the example gives exactly one pair.

statement: You swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig. Does an effect that triggers 'when you steal a Gig' trigger?
why: 6.7.2: "A swap is not considered stealing, and doesn't trigger any effects related to stealing."

statement: You cannot choose a Gig die in your fixer area for an effect that says 'Increase a Gig by up to 2.'
why: 6.1.4: "You can't target Gig dice in the fixer area to fulfill or resolve effects."

statement: Your deck has the Legends V: Streetkid and V: Corporate Exile. The deck is legal.
why: 7.3.1: "You cannot use multiple Legends with the same name"; both are named V (3.9.4: subtitle is not part of the name).

statement: Can your main deck contain 51 non-Legend cards?
why: 7.3.2: "no fewer than 40 and no more than 50 cards."

statement: Your main deck already has 3 copies of Mantis Blades. You may not add a fourth copy, even one with a different card number.
why: 7.3.3: no more than three copies "(even if they have different card numbers)."

statement: You are going first. All three of your Legends start ready.
why: 7.7.4: "The player going first spends their 2 left-most Legends."

statement: The second player wants to mulligan before the first player has declared. May they?
why: 7.9.2: the first player "must declare... before the second player may declare and execute their own mulligan."

statement: After using your mulligan, you cannot mulligan your new opening hand again.
why: 7.9.2: "You have up to one (1) opportunity to mulligan your opening hand."

statement: In your Start Phase, do you draw before you ready your spent cards?
why: 8.6 lists 8.6.3 Ready before 8.6.4 Draw, in order.

statement: In your Start Phase, you ready your cards before you remove effects that last 'until the start of your next turn'.
why: 8.6.2.1 removes those effects in step 8.6.2, before 8.6.3 readies.

statement: Your fixer area has the d12 and d20 left. Can you roll in the d20?
why: 8.6.5.1.1: "You may only choose the d20 if there are no other Gigs in your fixer area."

statement: Partway through your Main Phase you notice you never drew for turn. May you keep taking new actions and draw later?
why: 8.7: "immediately complete any previous missed actions before taking any new ones."

statement: During your Main Phase, may you attack before playing any cards?
why: 8.10: "you may take valid Main phase actions in any order."

statement: You sold a card for turn. Can you use Sell for Turn again this turn?
why: 8.11.1: "You may only take the 'Sell for Turn' action once per turn."

statement: Can you Call a Legend during the React Step of your Rival's attack?
why: 8.12.2: "You may also 'Call a Legend' during the React Step during your Rival's turn."

statement: A Unit you played this turn has a [Spend Icon] effect. Can you activate it this turn?
why: 8.14.1: "You cannot activate [Spend Icon] effects on Lagging Units."

statement: At your end of turn, 'this turn' effects are removed before 'at the end of your turn' effects resolve.
why: 8.16 orders them: 8.16.1 resolves end-of-turn effects, then 8.16.2 removes 'this turn' effects.

statement: Units do not lose Lag until the start of their controller's next turn.
why: 11.3.2: "At the end of each turn, all Units lose the 'Lag' condition."

statement: Your ready Unit wants to attack a ready rival Unit. That target is valid.
why: 9.3.2.1: "A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target." A ready Unit is not.

statement: Your spent Unit can attack the rival Gig area.
why: 9.3.1: choose "a friendly ready Unit"; a spent Unit can't be chosen.

statement: You have no valid attack targets this turn. Can you still declare an attack to trigger [ATTACK] effects?
why: 9.3.2.4: "If there are no valid targets, you cannot attack."

statement: An effect lets your Unit attack ready Units. Does that also lift a separate restriction that it can't attack this turn?
why: 9.3.2.3.1: such an effect "does not remove other attack restrictions."

statement: Your [ATTACK] effect defeats the defending Unit before the React Step. The attack goes on to the React Step anyway.
why: 9.6: if "the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends."

statement: You are the attacking player. Can you take reactions during the React Step?
why: 9.7.1: reactions only "if you are the defending player."

statement: A ready Unit with [BLOCKER] redirects an attack. Does it become the defending Unit in place of the original target?
why: 9.9.1: "it becomes the defending Unit, fully replacing the previous attack target."

statement: A Unit with [BLOCKER] is already the target of an attack. It cannot use [BLOCKER] to redirect that attack to itself.
why: 11.28.3.1: "A Unit can't redirect an attack to itself if it's already the target of that attack."

statement: Your attacker has power 0 and attacks a Gig area. It steals 1 Gig.
why: 9.20.1.1: "If the attacking Unit has power 0, it steals 0 Gigs."

statement: Your attacker has power 14. Does it steal 2 Gigs?
why: 9.20.1.2: "A Unit with power 10 to 19 steals 2 Gigs."

statement: Your power-21 Unit attacks a Gig area holding only 2 Gigs. Because it should steal 3, it steals none.
why: 9.20.1.3: if it steals more than are there, "choose as many Gigs as possible to steal."

statement: A fight ends in a tie at 5 power each. Both Units lose.
why: 11.4.1.3: "neither Unit wins and both Units lose the fight."

statement: A power-0 Unit wins a fight because of a card effect. Does it defeat the opposing Unit?
why: 11.4.2.3.2: "Units with power 0 cannot defeat a Unit in a fight."

statement: The attacking Unit is removed from the field mid-fight after losers are declared. The defender that lost is still defeated by it.
why: 11.4.2.3.1: "Even if the opposing Unit is no longer on the field... it still defeats the loser."

statement: A Unit loses a fight but an effect says it can't be defeated in a fight. Does it still count as having lost?
why: 11.4.2.3.4: "that Unit still loses the fight, it only ignores the resulting defeat."

statement: While stealing, can an effect change a chosen Gig's value before it changes control?
why: 11.5.1.2: "A Gig's value can't change during stealing"; adjust before choosing or after the control change.

statement: Your attacker steals 2 Gigs. Must you choose both Gigs at the same moment?
why: 11.5.1.4.2: "choose the Gigs one at a time."

statement: When your attacker steals, you are not required to take the highest-value Gig in the defending area.
why: 11.5.1.4.1: "You may choose to steal any Gig in the defending Gig area, regardless of its value."

statement: While one of your effects is resolving, can you activate another effect partway through?
why: 10.2.3: "you cannot play cards, activate effects, or resolve other pending effects until the current effect finishes resolving."

statement: An effect tells you to defeat a rival Unit, but your Rival has no Units. The controlling player picks nothing and the effect is invalid.
why: 10.7: "If an effect requires a target or choice with no legal options, the effect is invalid."

statement: An activated effect needs a target as part of its activation cost, and every possible target is illegal. You cannot activate it.
why: 10.8: "the effect is invalid and you cannot activate it."

statement: Your pending effect's target leaves play before it resolves. Do you still resolve as much as possible?
why: 10.10: "If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible."

statement: You have three pending effects. Must you resolve them in the order they triggered?
why: 10.12: "If you have multiple pending effects, you may resolve them in any order."

statement: Both players control pending effects. They take turns, resolving one effect each.
why: 10.13: "the turn player resolves all their pending effects before their Rival resolves all of theirs."

statement: An [ATTACK] trigger checks 'if this Unit has power 5+.' It had power 3 when triggered but 5 when it resolves. Does the condition succeed?
why: 10.16.1.1: extra conditions "do not need to be true when it triggers, only when you resolve it."

statement: A Unit with 'when this Unit steals a Gig, draw 1' steals 2 Gigs at once. The effect does not become pending twice.
why: 10.16.3: the effect "becomes pending once for each time that condition is met"; 2 Gigs means twice.

statement: You can't pay every activation cost of an effect. Can you pay the ones you can and activate it?
why: 10.19.2: "If you can't pay all required costs, you cannot activate the effect."

statement: You activate an effect on a Unit, and the Unit leaves the field before the effect resolves. The effect is cancelled.
why: 10.21: "it resolves even if its source leaves the area it was in."

statement: A persistent effect does not become pending when its condition becomes true.
why: 10.22.2: "A persistent effect never becomes pending."

statement: When a replacement effect applies, the process it replaces does not happen.
why: 10.25: "The replaced action or process does not occur at all."

statement: A replacement effect is optional. May its controller choose not to apply it?
why: 10.26: "the player who controls that replacement effect may choose not to apply it."

statement: An effect asks you to choose 3 targets but only 2 are valid. The whole effect fails.
why: 10.31.2: "choose as many valid targets as possible up to that number instead."

statement: An effect asks you to choose a number. Can you pick -2?
why: 10.31.3: "that player must choose a non-negative whole number."

statement: A cost-reduction effect does not stop at 1 €$ when it lowers what you pay to play a card.
why: 11.11.3: reductions "cannot reduce the amount below 1 €$."

statement: You play a card for free. Do cost-increase effects make you pay anything?
why: 11.11.4.2: "ignore effects that increase or reduce the amount you pay to play it."

statement: A cost-reduction effect lowers what you pay for a card. Its cost value is unchanged.
why: 11.11.2: such effects "do not change the card's cost value".

statement: An effect makes you sell two cards at once. You put both into the Eddies area together as a single sale.
why: 11.12.1.2: "you must sell each card individually."

statement: A sold card enters the Eddies area face-down and ready.
why: 11.12.1.1: "it enters the Eddies area face-down and ready."

statement: A card effect puts a card with no Sell Tag into your Eddies area. Is that allowed?
why: 11.12.2.1: such a card "isn't required to have an Eddie symbol."

statement: You Call a face-down Legend that is spent. It does not stay spent when it flips face-up.
why: 11.14.1.3: "The called Legend maintains its orientation (spent or ready) when flipped face-up."

statement: You Called a Legend in your Main Phase. Can you Call another during your Rival's React Step this same turn?
why: 11.14.2: "You may only Call a Legend once per turn."

statement: An effect says 'Draw up to 3'. May you draw one card, look at it, and then decide whether to draw more?
why: 11.8.2.2: "choose the number of cards you will draw, then draw exactly that number of cards."

statement: An effect tells you to bottom-deck your Rival's card. Do you bottom-deck it into your own deck?
why: 11.15.1.2: "If you would bottom-deck a card you don't own, its owner bottom-decks it instead."

statement: An effect bottom-decks several of your cards without saying 'in any order'. You do not choose their order.
why: 11.15.1 places them "in a random order"; only 11.15.2's 'in any order' lets you choose.

statement: A search effect looks at your top 2 cards, trashes 1, and says nothing about the other. May you add the other one to your hand?
why: 11.17.2: with no instruction, "return the cards to their original location in the same order."

statement: You search your deck for a Gear and find two. Can you choose not to reveal either?
why: 11.17.4.1: "you may purposely fail to find any or all target(s)."

statement: You spend a Unit to declare an attack. That does not activate the Unit's [Spend Icon] effect.
why: 11.19.2: spending "for any other reason... does not activate the [Spend Icon] effect."

statement: A Unit with [ADRENALINE] can attack while lagging.
why: 11.27.2: "Units with [ADRENALINE] may attack even if they're lagging."

statement: A [QUICK] effect may be used only during the React Step.
why: 11.30.2: "You may activate a [QUICK] effect as an action during your Main Phase or as a reaction".

statement: A [QUICK] effect used during the React Step does not require you to pay its cost.
why: 11.30.3: "You must still pay any associated costs no matter when you play the effect."

statement: A Unit's [DEFEATED] effect checks its equipped state. You use its information from when it was last on the field.
why: 11.23.3: "use the information from when the piece was last on the field".

statement: You play V: Streetkid with [Go Solo] from your Legends area. Can it attack the turn you play it?
why: 11.29.1: [GO SOLO] means "It can attack this turn", overriding the normal Lag on entry.

statement: V: Streetkid was played with [Go Solo] and is then defeated. It does not stay in your trash.
why: 11.29.1: "If it leaves the field, remove it from the game"; 4.4.1 agrees for Legends in invalid areas.

statement: Ruthless Lowlife is ready and your Rival has a Gig area with Gigs. Can it attack that Gig area?
why: Its text "can only attack rival Units"; 9.3.2.3 lets card effects restrict valid targets.

statement: Swordwise Huscle attacks with power 3, gains +2 before its [Attack] trigger resolves, and you draw 1.
why: Its text checks "If this Unit has power 5+"; 10.16.1.1 says that's checked on resolution, when it is 5.

statement: Johnny Silverhand: Never Stop Fighting fights a CORPO Unit that has higher power. Does Johnny win?
why: Its text: "This Unit wins all fights against CORPO Units"; 11.4.1.4 says card text supersedes power comparison.

statement: Animals Wrecker (power 10) attacks a Gig area with 3 Gigs. It steals 2 Gigs.
why: 9.20.1.2: "A Unit with power 10 to 19 steals 2 Gigs."

statement: You sell Mantis Blades for turn. Mantis Blades has a Sell Tag, so the sale is allowed.
why: Mantis Blades has a Sell Tag; 8.11 lets you reveal and sell such a card once per turn.

statement: Johnny Silverhand: Never Stop Fighting cannot be sold for an Eddie.
why: It has no Sell Tag (the errata confirms it "cannot be sold"); 3.12.1 requires a Sell Tag to sell from hand.

statement: Deadman Transmitter is equipped to your Unit, which would be defeated. Is the Gear defeated instead of the Unit?
why: Its text is a replacement; 10.25 says the replaced process "does not occur at all."

statement: Detonate is in your hand when a rival Unit attacks you. May you play it during the React Step?
why: Detonate has [Quick]; 9.10.1 lets you play a [QUICK] Program as a reaction.

statement: You play Over the Edge when your friendly d20 shows 7. Can it defeat a power-9 Unit?
why: Its text targets power "equal to or less than the value of a friendly d20"; 9 > 7, so it isn't a legal target (10.7).

statement: Royce: Don't Call Me Simon is played while you have less Street Cred than your Rival. It can defeat a rival Unit with power 3.
why: The power-3 upgrade is a condition: "If you have more Street Cred than a Rival"; it's false, so only power 2 or less (10.3).

statement: You play Minotaur but have equal Street Cred with your Rival. Does its [Play] effect defeat a rival Unit?
why: Its text requires "more Street Cred than a Rival"; 10.3.1: "If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect."

statement: Octant's printed cost is 7. You control three Gigs with 8+ value, so its cost value becomes 4.
why: 11.11.2: reductions "do not change the card's cost value"; you pay 4, but its cost stays 7.

statement: Industrial Assembly resolves when no friendly Gig can reach 8+. Do you still increase a Gig and skip the draw?
why: You resolve as much as possible (2.4); the draw's condition is false, so per 10.3.1 it doesn't apply.

statement: Japantown Jonin has power 0 and attacks a Gig area. It steals 0 Gigs.
why: 9.20.1.1: "If the attacking Unit has power 0, it steals 0 Gigs."

statement: Secondhand Bombus, power 0, uses [Blocker] and fights a power-3 attacker. Does Secondhand Bombus defeat the attacker?
why: 11.4.2.3.2: "Units with power 0 cannot defeat a Unit in a fight."

statement: Augmented Negotiators uses [Blocker]. Your Rival then discards 1.
why: Its text triggers "When this Unit uses [Blocker], a Rival discards 1." 11.28.2 allows [Blocker] during the React Step.

statement: Offduty Malfini enters play. Its [Play] spends itself and a rival Unit, which makes that rival Unit a valid attack target.
why: Its text spends a rival Unit; 9.3.2.1: "A spent rival Unit is a valid attack target."

statement: MaxTac Suppression Team is in play. A rival Unit with [Adrenaline] is played. Can it attack this turn?
why: Its text: "Rival Units can't attack the turn they're played." 2.6: "the preventing effect always takes precedence."

statement: Trauma Team Operatives costs 6 and you have 7 Units in your trash. You play it for 0 €$.
why: Its text floors the reduction at "a minimum of 1 €$", as does 11.11.3.

statement: Adam Smasher: Metal Over Meat's [Play] does not defeat Adam Smasher itself.
why: Its text defeats "all other Units"; 10.1.4 ties 'this' wording to the source, and 'other' excludes it.

statement: Alt Cunningham: Mother of Daemons lets you discard a card with cost equal to a stolen Gig's value. If you do, is the Gig not stolen?
why: 11.5.1.5's example is this effect: the Gig "isn't stolen" once you discard.

statement: You equip Mandibular Upgrade to a Unit with printed power 3. The Gear does not change the Unit's power.
why: Mandibular Upgrade has power 0; 3.17.2 adds Gear power to printed power, so the Unit stays at 3.

statement: Safety Override is played, then your Unit loses a fight. Is the opposing rival Unit defeated?
why: Its text: "The next time a friendly Unit loses a fight this turn, defeat the opposing rival Unit."

statement: Corpo Security is ready with no restrictions on its target. Can it attack?
why: Its text: "This Unit can't attack." 9.3.1 requires a Unit "that can attack".

statement: Tyger's Whisper's [Play] lets you Call a Legend for free, but you already Called one this turn. Can you Call again?
why: 5.7.3: Call a Legend "may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to".

statement: Riding Nomad has [Adrenaline]. Can it attack the turn it is played?
why: 11.27.1: [ADRENALINE] means "This Unit can attack the turn it's played."

statement: Riot Shield's text makes your Rival pay +2 €$ to use [Go Solo]. A Rival Go Solos a 5-cost Legend. They pay 7.
why: Its text adds +2 €$ to the 5-cost Go Solo; 11.1.2: "A cost must be paid in full".

statement: Sandevistan is equipped to your Unit. At the end of your turn, the Unit readies.
why: Its text readies "At the end of your turn"; 8.16.1 resolves those effects.

statement: Corporate Surveillance targets a cost-5 rival Unit. Can it spend that Unit?
why: Its text: "Spend a rival Unit with cost 4 or less." A cost-5 Unit is not a legal target.

statement: Modded Kusanagi has [Adrenaline]. You play it and attack the same turn.
why: 11.27.1: [ADRENALINE] means "This Unit can attack the turn it's played."

statement: At the end of your turn, Modded Kusanagi returns to its owner's hand. Its equipped Gear does not stay on the field.
why: 4.12: "all of its equipped Gear moves with it."

statement: Jacked-In Voodoo Boy is ready and you have not played a Program this turn. Can it attack?
why: Its text: "can't attack unless you played a Program this turn."

statement: Delamain: Rideshare AI is played. Do you draw 2?
why: Its [Play] draws 2; 11.24.1: [PLAY] means "When you play this card".

statement: MT0D12 Flathead has a Sell Tag. Can you sell it for turn?
why: MT0D12 Flathead has a Sell Tag; 8.11 lets you sell such a card once per turn.

statement: Floor It gives a rival Unit -1 power this turn. Your Rival's Unit had power 1. It now fights as power 0.
why: 1 - 1 = 0 power, and 2.10.1 treats values 0 or below as 0 for comparisons.

statement: Reboot Optics is played, and the next rival Unit wins its fight. Is your Unit defeated?
why: Its text: the rival Unit "doesn't defeat the opposing friendly Unit." 11.4.2.3.4: it still lost, defeat ignored.

statement: Lizzy Wizzy: Delicate Weapon plays a Program from your trash for free. Do you still pay that Program's cost?
why: 11.11.4: "When you play a card 'for free,' play the card without paying its cost."

statement: Alt Cunningham: Soulkiller Architect plays a Program from your trash for free.
why: Its text says "(You still pay its cost.)"; 3.11.1.1 requires paying unless an effect says 'for free'.

statement: You play Unlikely Bond while all your Units are spent. It does not bottom-deck a spent rival Unit.
why: Its text: "If you do, bottom-deck a spent rival Unit." You didn't, so per 10.3.1 that part doesn't apply.

statement: Les Élémens bottom-decks your Rival's lowest-power Unit. Two rival Units tie for lowest. Do you choose which?
why: Its text: "(If there are multiple, choose 1.)"; 10.31 says choices are made as instructed.

statement: Muamar Reyes: El Capitán's [Call] effect is chosen to make a Unit unable to be defeated in a fight. The Unit loses a fight. Did it lose?
why: 11.4.2.3.4: "that Unit still loses the fight, it only ignores the resulting defeat."

statement: Hanako Arasaka: Daughter of the Emperor swaps a friendly Gig with a rival Gig. The swap does not count as stealing.
why: 6.7.2: "A swap is not considered stealing".

statement: Saburo Arasaka: Stubborn Patriarch gives friendly ARASAKA Units +1 while attacking. After the attack ends, does that +1 still apply?
why: 9.24: after an attack ends, "remove effects that last 'while attacking'".

statement: A 16-year-old wants to enter an Organized Play event. May they participate?
why: TR 2.1.1: "Players who are less than 17 years old may not participate in Organized Play."

statement: At a competition-level event, your decklist lists a 45-card main deck, 3 Legends and a 7-card sideboard. That is a legal decklist composition.
why: TR 2.1.3: "Exactly 3 Legend Cards" and "40-50 Card Main Deck + 0 or 7 Card Sideboard".

statement: A player uses a spindown d20 as a Gig die. Is that legal?
why: TR 2.1.4: "spindown" dice "are not legal for play".

statement: Card sleeves are required at a casual Night City Brawl.
why: TR 2.1.5: sleeves are required at competition-level events and Night City Showdowns; "At all other casual-level events, players are not required".

statement: During a match you write down your Rival's card names in your notes. Is that allowed?
why: TR 2.1.6: "Players may not transcribe card names" in notes.

statement: A spectator notices a gameplay error. They should report it to a judge rather than tell the players.
why: TR 2.1.7: "If a spectator notices an error... they should report it to a judge"; spectators may never act on gameplay.

statement: A judge working a Night City Showdown also plays in it.
why: TR 2.2.1: judges at Showdowns or competition-level events "may not participate in these events while also acting as a Judge."

statement: A Floor Judge wants to issue a game loss. Must the Head Judge approve it?
why: TR 2.2.1.2: for a game loss or more severe, the Floor Judge "must discuss the penalty with the Head Judge and receive their approval."

statement: A ruling takes 5 minutes to settle. The Floor Judge should give a time extension.
why: TR 2.2.1.2: "Floor Judges should provide a time extension if a ruling or investigation takes longer than 3 minutes."

statement: You play cards printed in Japanese at an English-region event. Rulings follow the English printing.
why: TR 2.4.4: "Judge rulings and game clarifications must be done in accordance with the English printing".

statement: At an Edgerunners Open Regional single-elimination round, may players agree to an Intentional Draw?
why: TR 3.2.2: "Players may not choose to ID during a single elimination round."

statement: In a single-elimination round, the higher seed chooses who goes first rather than rolling a die.
why: TR 3.2.2: "the player with the higher seed will choose the player going first or second as opposed to a random method".

statement: Your Rival refuses a takeback you asked for. May you call a judge?
why: TR 3.4.3: "If a player insists on receiving a rewind but their Rival disagrees, call a Judge."

statement: At a competition-level event, a judge grants a rewind because a player didn't know a Comprehensive Rule.
why: TR 3.4.3: "a player may not rewind gameplay due to lack of player knowledge" at competition level.

statement: You add a Legend card to your sideboard. Is that allowed?
why: TR 3.4.4: "Players may not sideboard Legend cards."

statement: After sideboarding, your main deck may have one more card than before.
why: TR 3.4.4: "the deck must still have the same number of cards as it did pre-sideboard".

statement: Round time is called in Swiss. Players finish the current turn, then each takes one more turn.
why: TR 3.4.5: "Finish the current turn", then "Both players will receive one full turn".

statement: During a Pre-Release, a judge deck-checks a player. A dice check happens at the same time.
why: TR 4.1.2: "when performing deck checks, Judges must also simultaneously perform dice checks."

statement: A player's triggered ability would have no impact on the game state and they skip it. Is that a Missed Trigger?
why: TR A.2.1: if it "would have no impact on the game state... it doesn't need to be acknowledged."

statement: A player draws seven cards for their opening hand. The infraction is a Hidden Zone Error.
why: TR A.2.1 lists "A player draws seven cards in their opening hand" under Hidden Zone Error.

statement: Two players roll a d20 to decide their match instead of playing. Both receive a match loss.
why: TR A.2.2 (Randomizing Match Result): "The player offering or both players engaging in the method receive a match loss."

statement: A player's deck contains 4 copies of one card. The listed penalty is a Warning.
why: TR A.2.2 lists "4 copies of a card" under Illegal Deck [Disqualification].

statement: A Warning is meant for first instances of a rules violation.
why: TR A.1.1: "generally to be given to first instances during tournament play of any rules being violated."

statement: A Game Loss issued after a match ends is applied to the first game of the next round, and that player may sideboard before that game.
why: TR A.1.2: "In such cases, the affected player may not sideboard before the game."

statement: A disqualified player keeps their spot in the standings.
why: TR A.1.4: they are "removed from the subsequent run of the tournament, including their place in the standings."

statement: Pre-Release decks must contain at least 30 cards.
why: TR D.2.1: "A player's main deck must contain at least 30 cards."

statement: In a Pre-Release, may your main deck include cards of a color your Legends don't give RAM for?
why: TR D.2.1: decks "may include any cards of those colors, ignoring RAM limits."

statement: A player in a 6-Pack sealed event brings only 2 Legends. They add a blank Eddie for the missing one.
why: TR D.2.2: "For every missing Legend... they add the top card of their deck face down as a blank Eddie".

statement: Pre-Release cards are legal at other events before their set's release.
why: TR 2.4.1: they "will not be legal for other events until their respective set is released."

statement: Signed cards may be used if the signature is undetectable from the back.
why: TR 2.4.1: signatures are allowed if "undetectable in any way except when looking at the face of the card."

statement: Sleeves for your Legends must match your main deck sleeves.
why: TR 2.4.2: Legends "must be sleeved to be distinguishable from main deck cards".

statement: An unofficial playmat with printed gameplay reminders is allowed at an Organized Play event.
why: TR 2.4.3: unofficial playmats "may not have game information such as gameplay reminders" printed.

statement: A Quick best-of-1 deck at a Night City Brawl has no sideboard.
why: TR C.2.2: "a constructed format legal best-of-1 deck with no sideboard".

statement: In competitive best-of-1, players get 3 minutes to pre-sideboard and may not touch their sideboard after.
why: TR C.2.1: "Once these three minutes have elapsed, players may not look at or exchange cards with their sideboard".

statement: Players may use a digital device during gameplay if it has no internet connection.
why: TR 2.1.5: devices may not be used "except if the device is not connected to any outside resources."

statement: An unofficial token's purpose must be told to your Rival right away.
why: TR 2.1.5: "its purpose must be communicated to the Rival immediately."

statement: A TO of a District Open plays in their own event.
why: TR 2.2.2.1: "TOs at Night City showdown or District Open competition-level events may not participate in any event they organize."

statement: Coverage teams may use AI-generated art in stream visuals.
why: TR 2.2.2.3: Coverage Teams "may not use AI-generated content for any visual materials".

statement: Adam Smasher: Ender of Legends is played with [Go Solo]. Its [Play] effect defeats a rival Unit.
why: Go Solo plays the card, so per 11.24.2 the [PLAY] trigger becomes pending once its play requirements are met.

statement: Royce: Psycho on the Edge has 2 Gears equipped. During your turn its power gains +4 from its text, plus the Gears' power.
why: Its text: "+2 power for each of its equipped Gear" during your turn; 3.17.2 adds Gear power and modifiers.

statement: Dexter DeShawn: Off the Grid cannot be played from your Legends area to the field.
why: It has a null cost and no [Go Solo]; 4.5.3: null-cost Legends "cannot be played to the field."

statement: Yorinobu Arasaka: Embracing Destruction is face-up. Your first ARASAKA Unit attacks this turn. Do you draw 1?
why: Its triggered text fires "The first time a friendly ARASAKA Unit attacks each turn"; 10.16.1 makes it pending when that happens.

statement: La Llorona: Ghost of the Past uses [Blocker]. Must you increase a Gig by at least 1?
why: Its text says "up to 3"; 2.8: with 'up to' "you can choose none or 0".

statement: Valentino Guerrera has more Street Cred than your Rival. It may attack a ready rival Unit with [Blocker].
why: Its text allows attacking "ready Units with [Blocker]" when you have more Street Cred; 2.5 says card text wins.

statement: 6th Street Recruits is in play. A friendly Unit steals a d8. You increase a Gig by up to 6.
why: Its text triggers only "When a friendly Unit steals a d6"; a d8 doesn't meet the trigger.

statement: Kerry Eurodyne: The Last Rockerboy entered the field last turn. It cannot use its [Spend] effect this turn.
why: 11.3.2: "At the end of each turn, all Units lose the 'Lag' condition", so it is no longer lagging.

statement: Meredith Stout: Stone Cold Corpo fights a Legend. Its power is 7 in that fight.
why: Its text gives +2 "while fighting a Legend"; 5 + 2 = 7, applied before the comparison (11.4.2.1).

statement: Chrome Fang's [Play] is active. A rival Unit with power 4 tries to steal a friendly Gig of value 6. Can it?
why: Its text: rival Units "can't steal friendly Gigs with value higher than their power"; 11.5.1.3 applies restrictions before selection.

statement: El Sombrerón: La Venganza Lenta attacks. You may pay 2 €$ to boost it. Paying is optional.
why: Its text: "You may pay 2 €$"; 2.1.1 lets you skip a 'you may' part.

statement: Screw: Lovelorn Fool is defeated with another Unit in your trash. Its [Defeated] effect cannot add any Unit to your hand.
why: Its text: "Add another Unit from your trash to your hand"; another Unit is there, so it can.

statement: V: Roamer of the Badlands steals 2 Gigs at once. Its increase effect resolves only once, for one of the Gigs.
why: 10.16.3: the effect "becomes pending once for each time that condition is met"; 2 Gigs, twice.

statement: Yorinobu Arasaka: Steel Dragon plays a cost-4 Unit for free. That Unit can attack rival Units this turn.
why: Units enter with Lag (4.7), but 9.3.2.3 lets card effects add attack permissions; its text says "It can attack rival Units this turn."

statement: Arasaka Emergency Radioport's Unit is spent after you already Called a Legend this turn. It does not let you Call another.
why: 11.14.2: "You may only Call a Legend once per turn", which the card repeats.

statement: Satori: Sword of Saburo is equipped and your Unit wins a fight against a rival Unit. Do you draw 1?
why: 4.11.3: bottom-textbox effects are inherited, so the Unit's win triggers the draw.

statement: All is Lost trashes 3 cards, none of them Units. Do you still trash the 3?
why: 10.6.2: ignore the invalid part "and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible"; the trash still happens.

statement: Appetite for Destruction is played. A friendly Unit later wins a fight by exactly 3 power. It does not also steal a Gig.
why: Its text needs a win "by 3+ power"; exactly 3 meets it, so the condition is true (10.3).

statement: Bonnie and Clyde is played when your Rival controls 2 more Gigs than you. May you defeat 2 rival Units with power 4 or less?
why: Its text: "You may defeat 2 instead if a Rival controls at least 2 Gigs more than you."

statement: Shattered Memories makes each player discard their hand. Your Rival discards before you, the turn player.
why: 10.2.2: "the turn player performs their actions first, followed by their Rival."

statement: Carnage at the Colosseum costs 6 and you control 2 Gigs with 8+. Do you pay 4 €$?
why: Its text: -1 €$ per 8+ Gig, so 6 - 2 = 4. 11.11.2: cost value stays 6.

statement: Rogue Amendiares: Preem Solo, played with [Go Solo], steals a Gig with value 4. Do you draw 1?
why: 4.2.1: on the field it's a Legend, so "When a friendly Legend steals a Gig, if its value is even, draw 1" applies.

statement: Kerry Eurodyne: Axe, Attitude, Audience is face-up. You cannot reroll a Gig you just rolled in from your fixer area.
why: Its text: "you may ignore the result and reroll it once" when you roll in a Gig (8.6.5).

statement: Viktor Vektor: Sit Down and Relax is Called and you find two cost-2 Gears. You cannot choose to add zero Gears.
why: Its text says "up to 2"; 2.8: with 'up to' "you can choose none or 0".

statement: Sketchy Ripper attacks and finds a Gear in the top 3. You are not allowed to fail to find it.
why: 11.17.4.1: searching a hidden area, "you may purposely fail to find any or all target(s)".

statement: Dexter DeShawn: One Last Chance attacks. Your Rival may react before its [Attack] Gig adjustment resolves.
why: 11.25.2.2: "Resolve all pending [ATTACK] effects before your Rival's react step."

statement: Maelstrom Goons steals a Gig while unequipped. Your Rival discards 1.
why: Its text: "if it's equipped, a Rival discards 1"; unequipped, the condition is false.

statement: Viktor Vektor: You Might Feel a Little Pinch plays a CYBERWARE Gear from your trash. Can it equip that Gear to itself?
why: 4.10.1 sets only the default targets; its text restricts: "Equip it only to another friendly Unit."

statement: Gilded Matón's [Play] lets you defeat a friendly Gear. You decline, so a rival Unit is not defeated.
why: Its text: "If you do, defeat a rival Unit"; you didn't, so per 10.3.1 that part doesn't apply.

statement: Hanako Arasaka: In a Gilded Cage searches the top 4. Unchosen cards go to the bottom of the deck.
why: Its text: "Bottom-deck the rest." 11.15.1 places them in random order.

statement: T-Bug: Amateur Philosopher is defeated after you already Called a Legend this turn. You do not get to look at your face-down Legends.
why: 2.4: resolve as much as you can; the look happens even though the Call can't (5.7.3).

statement: Caliber: Totentanz's Top Dog's [Play] targets a rival Unit with cost 3. Is it defeated?
why: Its text: "Defeat a rival Unit with cost 2 or less"; cost 3 isn't a legal target.

statement: Jackie Welles: Ride or Die Choom attacks with 2 even-value friendly Gigs. It gets +4 power this turn.
why: Its text: "+2 power this turn for each friendly Gig with an even value": 2 x 2 = 4.

statement: An effect gives you control of a rival Unit. You do not become its controller.
why: 1.7.3: "Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners"; you become controller, not owner.

statement: Overtime is underway and you reach 7 Gigs during your Main Phase. Must you wait for the start of your next turn to win?
why: 1.11: in overtime, with seven or more Gigs "at any point, you immediately win the game."

statement: You may concede during your Rival's turn.
why: 1.16: "At any point, you may concede."

statement: An effect has a cost you could pay, but you choose not to pay it. Are you forced to activate it anyway?
why: 2.7: "you may choose not to pay it and thus not activate the effect."

statement: A card named Pilar & Rebecca counts as a card named Rebecca.
why: 3.9.3: such a card "has 3 names: both contained names, plus the combined name."

statement: A Legend with a Sell Tag, face-up in your Legends area, can be spent to pay 1 €$.
why: 3.12.2: "Legends with a sell tag can be spent to pay 1 €$ while face-up in the Legends area."

statement: Your three Legends give 2 Green, 2 Green and 2 Red RAM. Your Green RAM Limit is 4.
why: 3.20.5.1: "A deck's RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends' RAM in that color."

statement: An equipped Legend moves from the field to your hand and is removed from the game. Its Gear is not removed from the game with it.
why: 4.12.2: the Gear "is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend".

statement: A card with a +2 power modifier enters a hidden area. It does not lose that modifier.
why: 5.3.2.2: "remove any existing modifiers attached to it."

statement: An effect lets you look at a face-down Legend. After it resolves, can you look again later?
why: 5.7.4.3: "you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unless otherwise specified."

statement: Several of your cards enter your trash at the same time. Your Rival chooses their order.
why: 5.9.4.1: "their owner adds them in any order."

statement: Your die roll lands cocked between faces. Do you re-roll it?
why: 6.2.4 requires a definitive result; 6.2.5: "ignore the result and roll it again properly."

statement: The player chosen by the random method must go first.
why: 7.5.2: they "decide... whether they will go first or second."

statement: Your Rival may shuffle your deck before the game.
why: 7.6.2: "Your Rival may cut or shuffle the deck for you, if they choose."

statement: In your Main Phase, between actions and with nothing pending, you cannot pass your turn.
why: 8.9: "while you are not taking an action, you may choose to pass your turn".

statement: During the React Step, the attacking Unit leaves the field. The attack does not end.
why: 9.13: "If at any point the attacker or the defending Unit is no longer in the field area, the attack ends."

statement: The rival Gig area has no Gigs when the Steal Step begins. Can any Gigs be stolen?
why: 9.19: "no Gigs can be or are stolen."

statement: An attack ends before reaching the Fight Step. Is a fight still held?
why: 9.22.1: "no fight happens and no Gigs are stolen."

statement: Pacifica Netrunner is played while your Street Cred is even. Its [Play] cannot stop a rival Unit from readying.
why: Its text: "If your Street Cred is an even number, a rival Unit can't ready until your next turn"; the condition is met (10.3).

statement: Field Operator is played while your Gig area is empty. Its [Play] does not draw a card.
why: 5.11.4.1: Null Street Cred "does not count towards even or odd values", so 'even' is false.

statement: Pepe Najarro: Working Doubles attacks with a value-pair of Gigs. May you ready up to 2 MERC Legends in your Legends area?
why: Its text: "ready up to 2 MERC Legends"; 2.8 lets you choose 0 to 2.

statement: MaxTac AV's [Play] swap of Gigs is optional.
why: Its text: "You may swap a friendly Gig with a rival Gig."

statement: Wraith Marauders, power 4, steals a Gig of value 4. Its effect may ready Wraith Marauders itself.
why: Its text readies "another friendly Unit"; 11.5.1.7 puts the trigger after the Gig moves.

statement: Nadia: Fighting Through Grief, played this turn, can attack the Rival's Gig area while the Rival controls more Gigs.
why: Its text grants that permission; 2.5 says card text overrides the Lag rule.

statement: Nadia: Fighting Through Grief, played this turn, can attack a spent rival Unit when the Rival controls more Gigs.
why: Its permission is only for "their Gig area"; 9.3.2.3.1 says it does not lift other restrictions like Lag.

statement: Panam Palmer: Strength Through Family lets you Call a Legend for free during your turn. You still can't Call more than once that turn.
why: 11.14.2: "You may only Call a Legend once per turn."

statement: MaxTac Heavy costs 7 and your Rival has 3 Units. Do you pay 4 €$?
why: Its text: -1 €$ per rival Unit: 7 - 3 = 4.

statement: Sandayu Oda: Hanako's Guardian cannot attack a spent rival Unit the turn it is played.
why: Its text: "This Unit can attack rival Units the turn it's played." 9.3.2.3.1 grants that permission.

statement: Saul Bright: Stormrider is attacking. Does it get +2 from its own text?
why: Its text gives "Other friendly Units" +2; that excludes itself.

statement: Zetatech Berserk costs 6 and you have 3 face-up Legends. Do you pay 3 €$?
why: Its text: -1 €$ per face-up Legend: 6 - 3 = 3.

statement: Peace Offering's set is optional; if you skip it but already control a value-pair, you still draw 1.
why: The draw's condition is checked when it resolves (10.3.3); you already control a value-pair, so you draw.

statement: Synapse Burnout is played in your Rival's React Step. Is that allowed?
why: It has [Quick]; 9.10.1 lets you play such a Program as a reaction.

statement: Memory Relapse spends a rival Unit, which then readies normally in your Rival's next Ready Step.
why: 8.6.3 readies spent cards, but its text says "It can't ready until your next turn"; 2.6: the preventing effect wins.

statement: We Gotta Live Together can be played for 3 €$ when your Rival controls at least 2 more Gigs.
why: Its text provides that alternate payment; 11.1.2.1 says pay the replacement cost.

statement: (Don't Fear) The Reaper spends all rival Units, then defeats one spent Unit.
why: 2.3: "Resolve card effects in the order they appear"; spending first makes targets available.

statement: Sasha Yakovleva: Won't Let You Down attacks and reveals a cost-5 card. The +5 power lasts through your Rival's next turn.
why: The gain is "this turn"; 8.16.2 removes 'this turn' effects at your end of turn.

statement: Evelyn Parker: Scheming Siren has power 0 and attacks a Gig area. It does not steal any Gigs.
why: 9.20.1.1: "If the attacking Unit has power 0, it steals 0 Gigs."

statement: Misty Olszewski: Mender of Broken Spirits can attack a spent rival Unit.
why: Its text: "This Unit can't attack."

statement: Delamain Cab didn't steal a Gig this turn. At end of turn, do you ready 1 Eddie?
why: Its text needs "if this Unit stole a Gig this turn", checked at resolution (10.3.3); it didn't.

statement: Hacked Corpo trashes 3 cards with no Programs among them. Do you still trash them?
why: 10.6.2: ignore the invalid part and resolve the rest; the trash still happens.

statement: Two effects trigger while one of yours is resolving. May you stop and resolve the new ones first?
why: 10.14: "Finish resolving the current pending effect before resolving any new pending effects."

statement: A Unit has +2 power while attacking from another card. Once the attack ends, the +2 stops.
why: 10.23's example: the bonus applies "from the moment the Unit attacks until the attack ends."

statement: A mandatory and an optional replacement effect could both apply to one process. The mandatory one does not apply first.
why: 10.28: "apply mandatory replacement effects before optional replacement effects."

statement: A replacement effect already applied to a process. Can that same replacement apply to it again?
why: 10.29.1: "that same replacement effect cannot apply to that same action or process again."

statement: A Unit is defeated by a Program, not a fight. Does an effect that refers to 'defeated in a fight' apply?
why: 11.4.2.3.3: it applies "only to defeats from the opposing Unit as a result of losing."

statement: An effect names a different actor to steal a Gig. That actor is the one stealing.
why: 11.5.1.1.2: "If an effect specifies a different actor, the specified actor is the one that steals."

statement: While its [DEFEATED] effect resolves, a defeated Unit is considered in the trash.
why: 11.6.2: "A defeated Unit is considered to be in the trash while resolving [DEFEATED] effects".

statement: A Unit moves from the field to your hand with its Gear. The Gear does not stop being equipped.
why: 11.9.1.2: Gear stays equipped "unless it (or the Unit/Legend...) ... moves outside of the Legends area or field."

statement: An effect says Trash 3. You do not trash the cards one at a time.
why: 11.10.2.1.1: "trash each card individually. Do not place multiple cards into your trash at once."

statement: An effect tells you to top-deck a card your Rival owns. Its owner top-decks it instead.
why: 11.16.1.2: "If you would top-deck a card you don't own, its owner top-decks it instead."

statement: A revealed card has been placed back face-down in your deck. Can you look at it again freely?
why: 11.18.4: "it is hidden and can no longer be looked at unless otherwise specified."

statement: A Legend's activation cost is '1 €$, [Spend Icon]'. Spending that Legend alone also covers the 1 €$.
why: 11.20.1.1's example: "you must spend this Legend and 1 other Eddie or Legend."

statement: A [CALL] effect becomes pending when you reveal the Called Legend.
why: 11.22.2: "becomes pending when you reveal the Called Legend."

statement: An effect other than the Call a Legend action flips a Legend face-up. Its [CALL] effect does not trigger.
why: 11.22.1: [CALL] means "When you flip this Legend face-up through the 'Call a Legend' action".

statement: A Unit has two trigger keywords, [PLAY] and [ATTACK], before one effect. It triggers on each attack too.
why: 10.17.1's example: it triggers on play "and also triggers each time the Unit attacks."

statement: An effect becomes pending, then the game state changes. Without a resolution condition, does it still resolve?
why: 10.15: "later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving".

statement: An activated effect does not have to wait for pending effects to resolve before you activate it.
why: 10.18.1: you cannot activate one "while any effects are pending resolution."

statement: An activated effect has two activation costs. May you pay them in any order you like?
why: 10.19.3: "pay them in the order that they appear."

statement: A condition in an effect is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
why: 10.3.3: "A condition within an effect's resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves."

statement: Your own face-down Eddies are not hidden from you; you may look at them.
why: 5.8.3.1: "You cannot look at face-down cards in the Eddies area."

statement: You play an invalid card by mistake. You undo the attempt and return to the previous legal state.
why: 11.7.1.2: "undo the play attempt and return the game to the previous legal game state as much as possible."

statement: Playing a card from your trash does not require an effect that allows it.
why: 11.7.2: "You can only play cards from your hand unless an effect instructs otherwise."

statement: Legends you spend for 1 €$ do not count as Eddies.
why: 5.7.2.1: "Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies."

statement: After an attack, the turn player's Main Phase continues.
why: 9.24: "The turn player's Main Phase continues."

statement: An attack target stops being valid for the attacker partway through. The attack ends.
why: 9.21.3: an attack ends if "The attack target is no longer a valid attack target for the attacking Unit."

statement: You have 2 €$ available and the effect's activation cost is 3 €$. Can you pay 2 and activate it anyway?
why: 11.1.2: "A cost must be paid in full; if you cannot pay all required costs, you cannot ... activate the effect".

statement: An effect tells you to 'trash up to 3'. May you choose to trash 0 cards?
why: 11.10.2.1.2: "choose the number of cards you will trash"; 2.8: with 'up to' "you can choose none or 0".

statement: You play a card for free. Do you still have to meet its other play conditions, such as a legal equip target for a Gear?
why: 11.11.4.1: "When you play a card for free, you must still meet any additional conditions outside of the cost."

statement: At an LGS-level event, Swiss rounds may be played as 30-minute best-of-1 matches.
why: TR 3.2.1: "At the LGS-level, Swiss rounds can be played as either 50-minute best-of-3 or 30-minute best-of-1 matches."

statement: Players at a competition-level Swiss round agree to an Intentional Draw after the game has started.
why: TR 3.2.1: an ID is chosen "at the start of a Swiss round, before decks are revealed and before time has started".

statement: Your Rival's attack targets your Unit. Can you Call a Legend as a reaction during the React Step?
why: 9.8: "You may Call a Legend as a reaction." (It still counts toward once per turn.)

statement: The defending player has taken one reaction and no effects are pending. Can they now end the React Step?
why: 9.12: "while not taking a reaction and while there are no effects pending resolution, the defending player may choose to end the React Step."

statement: A fight's defending Unit is defeated. Do triggers from the fight resolve before the fight ends?
why: 11.4.2.2.1: fight triggers "become pending. Resolve them after the fight ends."

statement: Your Legend has a null cost and an effect references its cost. The effect treats that cost as 0.
why: 3.11.2.3: "For effects that reference a Legend's cost, a null cost is considered 0."

statement: A value of null ( - ) counts as an even number.
why: 2.10.2: null "does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd."
